name: Mam nhum
summary: Black sea urchin fermented in salt for 10 to 15 days into a smooth, thick, cloudy-red paste, salty, sour, and sweet with garlic and peppercorns. It was once sent to the king, and families often keep it rather than sell it.
origin: Xã Mỹ An, huyện Phù Mỹ.
texture: The finished ferment is smooth, thick, and a cloudy red, after 10 to 15 days in salt.
taste: It names salt, sour, and sweet inside the urchin's own taste. The seasoning is garlic and whole peppercorns.
howToEat: Eat it with fresh noodles, or as a dip for herbs and pork belly rolled in rice paper.
Families make it to keep and to give away, so a jar is not always for sale.
seoTitle: Mam nhum — fermented urchin in Phu My
seoDescription: Mắm nhum is black sea urchin fermented into a thick red paste in Mỹ An, Phù Mỹ, eaten with noodles or herbs and pork.
